design_decisions.question: Free/path calls, method calls, or both?
design_decisions.decision: Free/path calls ONLY this wave. A free/path call's callee spelling explicitly names its qualifying module/type (`fs::read`, `File::open`), giving a real, checkable signal. A method call's spelling (`method_call.method.to_string()`) carries NO qualifying information about the receiver's type at all -- `socket.read_to_string(..)` and a real `File`'s `.read_to_string(..)` are textually identical, and this extractor cannot tell them apart without type resolution it doesn't have. Persistence.rs's own module doc comment already names this exact ambiguity for its own method-call spellings ('game.commit(), ui.flush(), cache.sync() ... exactly as persistence-shaped by spelling as a real durable API call'); rather than accepting the same ambiguity for filesystem detection, this wave excludes method calls entirely as an explicit, documented scope boundary, verified by a dedicated negative test.

design_decisions.question: How to avoid the 'fs' substring collision risk (prefs::, myfs::, overlayfs::, ...)?
design_decisions.decision: Split the spelling on `::` and require the segment immediately before the final one to be EXACTLY `fs` (or `File`) -- never a substring match. This is the identical word-boundary discipline `max_structural_recursion_risk`'s own `as`-keyword scan already established for an identical collision risk (`task`/`class`/`database`/`phase` all contain "as" as a substring but must never trigger that guard). Verified directly by `filesystem_lookalike_module_names_do_not_false_positive`.

design_decisions.question: Which specific fs/File spellings to recognize, and why not attempt an exhaustive catalog?
design_decisions.decision: A deliberately bounded, well-known initial set (fs::read/read_to_string/read_to_end/read_dir/read_link/metadata/symlink_metadata/canonicalize -> Read; fs::write/create_dir/create_dir_all/remove_file/remove_dir/remove_dir_all/rename/copy/hard_link/symlink/set_permissions -> Write; File::open -> Read; File::create/create_new -> Write) -- comparable in size and restraint to persistence.rs's own 5-entry set, not an attempt to enumerate every std::fs function or every async-runtime fs module's full surface in one generation. Network/process/FFI/persist/event/auth/alloc/free/external-IO categories remain explicitly unmaterialized, left for future generations.

design_decisions.question: Refactor emit_panic into a general emit(), or duplicate the emission logic for the new categories?
design_decisions.decision: Refactored `emit_panic(mac)` into `emit(span, category)` (parameterized, called by both the Panic call site and the new filesystem call site) -- avoiding a second near-duplicate copy of the identical evidence/observation-emission logic, consistent with this session's own repeated architecture-quality discipline (StatementWalker, join_continuation, persistence_kind_for_spelling, ...).
